intent: A behind-the-scenes fix to the automated checks that publish these release notes - the app itself is unchanged.

title: YouTube downloads work again
intent: Downloads had started failing across the board as YouTube changed things on their end. FileTube now ships a much fresher downloader engine, configured the way the new YouTube requires - your failed subscriptions retry themselves on the next check.

title: Choose your downloader engine
intent: A new Downloads section in Setup lets you point FileTube's YouTube downloader at the newest stable or nightly engine release, so you no longer wait for a FileTube update when YouTube changes things. The engine that ships with the app always stays as the safety net: every new engine is health-checked before it takes over, a broken one switches back automatically and rings the bell, and a daily auto-update is there if you want it (off unless you turn it on).

title: Easier-to-tap card buttons on your phone
intent: The little action buttons on video cards (share, queue, delete, and friends) are now about a third bigger on phones, with a more forgiving tap area around each one - so you press the thing you meant to press. Desktop looks exactly the same.

title: Safer releases behind the scenes
intent: Every FileTube release is now started up and checked before it is published, and the exact copy that was checked is the copy you download. FileTube also keeps watch over the building blocks it is made from: known security problems now block a release until they are fixed, and updates to those building blocks arrive as tidy weekly proposals. Nothing changes in how you use the app - four such problems were found and fixed as part of building this.

title: Search finds channels now
intent: Searching for a channel's name now finds that channel's videos - even when they live in a folder with a different name, came from a one-off download, or you renamed the folder yourself. Search results also get a small All / Titles / Channels filter, so you can point your search at just video titles or just channel names, YouTube-style. Everything you could find before, you still find.

title: A tidier search toolbar on phones, and a clear button
intent: On phones, the search results toolbar now fits on one neat swipeable row instead of stacking a third row of buttons. And the search box gets a little X on the right - one tap empties it so you can type your next search, no more select-all-and-delete.

title: Open Stats without stopping your music
intent: Playing a video or track and want to peek at your library stats? Tapping Stats used to stop whatever was playing. Now it keeps right on going in the mini-player, just like every other page in the app, and the Stats item lights up in the sidebar while you're there.

title: A cleaner way to get around Settings
intent: Settings, Stats, and Subscriptions got a fresh menu. Instead of one long page of sections you expand and collapse (and lose your place in), each page is now a tidy list with a little icon for every section - tap one and just that section opens, with a back button to return. On a computer the list sits alongside the section you're viewing. Everything that was there is still there, just easier to find, and the Appearance section's icon even changes to match the retro era you've picked.

title: Your music keeps playing when you open Settings
intent: A few finishing touches to the new menus. The big one: opening Settings from the You menu on your phone no longer stops whatever you're playing - it keeps going in the mini-player, like everywhere else. Each menu page now opens with a friendly header that says what the page is for. Settings is just called "Settings" now. And you can jump straight to Stats and Subscriptions from the You menu on your phone, without digging through the side menu.

title: Menu header lines up, and Subscriptions is back in the You menu
intent: Two small fixes to yesterday's menu update. The header box at the top of each Settings-style page now lines up neatly with the rows beneath it instead of sitting slightly narrow. And Subscriptions is reliably in the You menu on your phone now - before, it could go missing right after the app first opened.

title: Tidier headers when you open a settings section
intent: When you tap into a section (like Appearance or Downloads) on your phone, the header now looks like a proper iOS screen: the title is centered with a clean back arrow on the left, instead of the title being squished next to the back button. A small thing that makes the menus feel a lot more finished.

title: Subscriptions that scale, and a tap-to-open channel page
intent: The Subscriptions list is built for a big library now. There's a search box at the top to find a channel instantly, the list is grouped into A-Z sections, and there's an A-Z strip down the side to jump straight to a letter - no more endless scrolling to reach the ones near the bottom. Tap any channel and its settings slide in as their own page, with the name centered and a back arrow to slide back. This is the first half of the Subscriptions makeover; more is on the way.

title: Fix: channel names were squished to one letter per line
intent: A quick fix to yesterday's Subscriptions update. On a large library the channel list was getting badly squeezed - each name stretched down the screen one letter at a time - because the 'Hide subscriptions' button was crowding the list sideways. The list now uses its full width again, so channel names read normally.

title: A cleaner Subscriptions page with a simple button bar
intent: The Subscriptions page got its final makeover. Instead of the old menu, there's now a tidy row of buttons across the top - Check all, One-off, Activity, and Add - and each one slides open its own clean page. The channel list stays front and center with its search and A-Z jump strip. All the power-user upkeep buttons (refresh avatars, reheat, and so on) are tucked neatly into Activity, and the old 'Hide subscriptions' button is gone, so the A-Z strip no longer floats in empty space.

title: Tidied up the Subscriptions list
intent: Removed the A-Z letter strip that was running down the side of the Subscriptions list - it sat awkwardly in empty space and slid out of reach on a long list. The channel list now uses the full width, and the search box plus the A-Z section headers are all you need to find a channel.

title: A crisper cold start - no more jump and pop-in
intent: Polished how the app looks the instant it opens. The home page no longer lurches downward as your Continue watching/listening/reading rows load in - their space is held ahead of time. On iPhone, the menu and side icons appear instantly instead of blinking in a moment late. And a few pages that used to flash empty before filling - Settings' folder list, a podcast's episode list - now show a gentle placeholder while they load.

title: Two desktop polish fixes
intent: Fixed a desktop quirk where clicking a menu item on Settings or Stats made the section headings jump upward and stay bunched together until you reloaded the page - they now stay neatly spaced. And the little account picture in the top-right 'You' button now shows a soft shimmer while it loads instead of popping in from an empty circle.

title: Empty the trash in one tap, and see your storage at a glance
intent: Three handy additions. The Trash section now shows how many items are in it and how much space they're taking - and a new 'Empty trash' button clears the whole thing at once (it takes two taps, so a single misclick can't wipe it). Your total library size on disk now appears right in the 'You' menu, so the number you check most is no longer buried in Stats - tap it to jump straight there. And on the Settings page, the admin sections (Downloads, Users, Backup & Restore) now fade in smoothly instead of popping in a moment after the page loads.

title: Sort and filter your lists
intent: The lists that are really tables can now be sorted and filtered. On the Stats page, By folder, By channel, Books, and Duplicates each get tappable column headings - tap one to sort by name, number of items, length, or size, tap again to reverse - plus a search box to jump to a folder or channel fast. There's a new 'Videos & audio' table too, so you can sort your whole library by size or length right from Stats and find your biggest or longest files. The Users and Trash lists in Settings are sortable and searchable the same way. And these tables now fill the screen instead of squeezing into a small box that wasted half the page on your phone. The Duplicates list now shows the biggest space-wasters first.

title: Swipe back, and a few page polish fixes
intent: You can now swipe in from the left edge of the screen to go back a page - handy for backing out of a Stats section or Settings. A few Stats pages got the same fill-the-screen and sorting treatment as the others (Most watched is now a sortable table). The Subscriptions Activity view is tidier - the download history, failures, and maintenance buttons are now neat collapsible sections that start closed. The annoying bug where the top of a page was hidden under the top bar when you opened it is fixed. And the modern home feed finally has its own card-vs-list view toggle, matching the one in your download folders.

title: Smoother swipe-back and a couple of polish fixes
intent: Follow-ups to the swipe-back gesture and a few small touches. Swiping back from the left edge no longer makes the whole screen shake as it moves - it's smooth now, and normal scrolling stays just as quick. The card-vs-list button on the home feed no longer looks like it's always switched on. And the Subscriptions page gets its header back - a title and a short explainer at the top, matching the other pages.

title: A slightly bigger card/list button
intent: The card-vs-list button on the home feed was a touch smaller than the icons next to it. It's now sized to match, so the row of buttons at the top of the page looks even.

title: Swipe back from anywhere on the screen
intent: The swipe-to-go-back gesture no longer needs to start right at the very left edge - now you can start a left-to-right swipe from anywhere on the screen to go back a page. It's smart about it: swiping across something that scrolls sideways (like the filter strips on the Stats page) scrolls that instead, and a slightly diagonal scroll won't send you back by accident.

title: Delete from notifications, instant resume, and a few fixes
intent: Four handy improvements. You can now delete a video straight from its notification - tap the trash button, tap again to confirm, and it goes to the Trash just like deleting it from a card, so you can clear out downloads you already know you don't want without opening them. The search box now clears itself after a search that finds something, so you can search the next thing without clearing it first (if a search finds nothing, it stays put so you can tweak it). The 'Resume playback?' countdown length is now yours to set in Settings - make it longer, shorter, or set it to zero to have videos resume instantly with no prompt at all. And a fix: playing a video at a faster speed and sending the app to the background no longer drops it back to normal speed - your 1.5x keeps going.

title: Groundwork for the background play/pause fix
intent: Some quiet groundwork toward a known issue: controlling playback from your headphones or the lock screen while a video plays in the background is unreliable. This release adds an on-screen diagnostic log (Settings, 'Show lifecycle debug log') that captures exactly what happens when a play/pause command comes in, so the actual cause can be pinned down and fixed properly. Nothing about normal playback changes.

title: Headphone play/pause works on the first press again
intent: Fixed: when a video is playing in the background, pausing from your AirPods or the lock screen now works on the first press. Before, the first press often did nothing (the system had the wrong idea of whether you were playing or paused) and you had to press twice. This is the fix the last release's diagnostic log helped track down.

title: Try-it setting for resuming background audio while locked
intent: A small fix and an opt-in experiment. The fix: the lock screen no longer shows 'Pause' when a resume didn't actually take, so the button always matches reality. The experiment (Settings, off by default): 'keep background video-audio controllable while locked' - when a video's audio is playing in the background, it keeps the app awake so you can un-pause it from your AirPods or the lock screen, which normally can't be done once the audio stops. It costs extra battery while playing in the background, so it's off unless you turn it on to try it.

title: Improving the keep-locked-controllable experiment
intent: A tune-up to the opt-in 'keep background video-audio controllable while locked' setting from the last release. It now works in a way iOS is more likely to honor for longer, so pausing and resuming from your AirPods or the lock screen should keep working past the first time, not just once. Still off by default and still uses extra battery while it's on - turn it on to try it.

title: Battery guard + tidier lock screen for the keep-locked setting
intent: Two polish touches to the opt-in 'keep background video-audio controllable while locked' setting. First, a battery guard: if you pause a backgrounded video and walk away, it now stops keeping the app awake after a few minutes instead of forever (so a forgotten video in your pocket won't drain the battery). Second, the lock-screen scrubber now shows the real video time instead of briefly flickering a little 0-to-3-second counter. Still off by default.

title: Delete videos straight from the Stats page
intent: You can now delete a video right from the Stats page instead of hunting for it on the main library. The 'Videos & audio' and 'Most watched' tables get a trash button on each row (tap once, tap again to confirm), and the Duplicates section lets you expand a group and remove the exact extra copies you don't want. Deletions go to the Trash, so they're recoverable, and the buttons only appear if your account can manage the library. Handy for pruning: sort by size, delete the biggest, done.

title: The keyboard shortcuts window fits without scrolling (plus a hidden toy)
intent: On a computer, the keyboard shortcuts window (press ?) now shows every shortcut in two columns so you can see them all at once without scrolling. On phones it looks the same as before. And a little easter egg: there are now four arrows tucked in the top-right corner of that window. Press your arrow keys, or click them, and each one plays a musical note so you can tap out a tune. Be the best FileTube FileTube Revolution player.

title: The DDR arrows are properly colored: left/right blue, up/down red
intent: A small tweak to the shortcuts-window easter egg: the four arrows are now colored on purpose and the same on every device - left and right are blue, up and down are red, like a real dance pad. Pressing an arrow still lights it up red. Before this they were either grey or whatever color your phone happened to pick.

title: DDR arrows flash by direction when you press them
intent: The shortcuts-window easter egg now flashes each arrow's square in its own color when you press it: left and right flash blue, up and down flash red, like a real dance pad. The arrows themselves stay a plain neutral color; only the square lights up.

title: Subtitles stay inside the video, even on your phone
intent: Fixed subtitles spilling out of the video on mobile: they were drifting up over the playback controls, and in the little corner mini-player they were huge and overflowed the frame. Now subtitles always sit inside the video picture, above the controls, and in the mini-player they shrink to fit neatly inside the thumbnail.

title: Settings sections open at the top, and Back remembers your spot
intent: Opening a section on the Settings, Stats, or Subscriptions pages (like Under the hood) used to land you partway down, with the section's title and back arrow hidden under the header. Now every section opens right at the top, and tapping Back returns you to the exact spot in the list you came from, the way the iPhone Settings app does.

title: The dance-pad easter egg comes to your phone
intent: The keyboard shortcuts window is now reachable on phones too: Stats has a Keyboard shortcuts entry that opens it, and the four little dance-pad arrows in its corner play their notes when you tap them - left and right flash blue, up and down flash red, just like on desktop. The shortcut list is there for reference; the arrows are the fun part.

title: Sneaky critter mode
intent: A completely optional bit of fun, off unless you turn it on: little critters peek out from behind cards and menus all around the app, tilted at cute angles - never over the video or music you're playing. Tap one and it makes a little noise and wiggles, shivers, or hops. Pick how many you want (an odd one, a tasteful smattering, or a little extreme) under Settings, Appearance. Three placeholder figurines are included; drop your own transparent images into the critters folder and they join in automatically, each with its own sound if you add a matching audio file.

title: The critters actually show up now
intent: Fixes Sneaky critter mode showing nothing at all: the critters were being drawn underneath the page background, so turning the mode on appeared to do nothing on any device. They now peek out from behind cards and menus the way they were meant to, on phone and desktop alike. Bonus: there are now five built-in placeholder figurines instead of three - a bunny, cat, bear, fox, and chick - until you drop your own images into the critters folder.

title: Critters visit the video page too
intent: Sneaky critters now show up on the page where you watch a video as well - peeking from behind the description box and the related-video thumbnails. They still never touch the video player itself.

title: Your own critter pictures now work when running in Docker
intent: If FileTube runs in Docker, pictures you dropped into the critters folder on your server were invisible to the app - it only saw its own built-in copies. The Docker setup now connects that folder to the app, so your own critters appear on the next refresh after updating. The folder's README also explains the one extra step for setups without a full code checkout.

title: Critters make it to the video page
intent: The page where you watch a video builds its content a moment after it opens, and the critters were only looking for hiding spots before that content arrived - so video pages stayed empty. The critters now check back a couple of times as the page fills in, then settle: within a second or two they peek out from behind the description and the related videos, and once placed they never jump around. Tip: the maximum number of critters on a page equals how many images are in your critters folder, so add more pictures to make the Obscene setting live up to its name.

title: Critters ambush from behind buttons, on every page
intent: The critters got sneakier and spread out. Instead of loitering behind big cards like wallpaper, they now favor popping out from behind buttons - shrunk down to button size, head and ears sticking out, properly cartoonish - and they roam every page now: subscriptions, history, books, music, podcasts, the comment box. They still never touch the player or the app's fixed menus, and tapping them works the same.

title: Critters commit to the bit
intent: Big critter glow-up. They now peek out from corners as well as edges, lean at wilder angles, face either direction, and vary how boldly they emerge - from a shy sliver to half a body. And the big one: a critter now hides behind exactly ONE thing - its own button or card - and sits on top of everything else nearby, so it never gets weirdly swallowed by a stray divider line the way the first ones did. Menus and popups still open on top of them, and they still never touch the video player.

title: Critters move into the feed
intent: On the phone's main feed, critters used to poke out the sides of the full-width cards and get chopped off by the screen edge, which looked like a glitch. Now anything full-width only lets them emerge from the top or bottom - so they climb out from behind a video's artwork onto its title, or peer down over the top of a card. Bonus: they can also hide behind the artwork itself, and keep an eye out for the tiny ones tucked behind a channel's little round avatar.

title: Critters that actually fit their hiding spots
intent: Three fit-and-finish fixes for critter mode. Critters now size themselves to whatever they hide behind, so a small button never has a giant peeking out with odd slices floating past its edges. When one emerges from underneath something, it now hangs upside-down with its head poking out - no more disembodied feet dangling below a card. And behind the little round channel avatars, the hidden part now follows the circle's curve instead of cutting a sharp straight edge through the critter.

title: Manage your critters from the browser
intent: Sneaky critters get their own Settings section, and admins get a full critter manager right in the app: upload new critter images and their tap sounds from any device, see the whole pool as little thumbnails, delete one critter or clear the pool (with a confirm tap so nothing goes by accident), and download everything as a zip for safekeeping. Dropping files straight into the folder still works exactly like before - the two ways stay in sync.

title: Critters follow you between Settings pages
intent: Opening a Settings section (or going back to the list) now gives the critters a fresh look at what's actually on screen, so they hide behind the page you're looking at instead of floating in mid-air where something used to be on the previous page.

title: Sneaky companions settle in properly
intent: The critter feature grows up into Sneaky companions - because what you upload can be critters, characters, or anything with a transparent background. Companions also stopped ending up on top of a page's title or channel name: on pages that load in stages, they now take a second look once everything has settled and tuck themselves properly behind their buttons. Plus a small copy cleanup throughout the feature.

title: Critters, cut clean
intent: The feature settles on its true name - just Critters - and gets its last visual rough edge filed off: a critter peeking from behind a button could sometimes show a hard slice floating in mid-air where the button doesn't even reach. Now the hidden part of every critter matches exactly what its hiding spot really covers, so every edge you see is the edge of something real.

title: Critters arrive with the page
intent: Critters no longer trail in after everything else has loaded. They now appear in the same moment the page's content does, their images are prepared ahead of time so the first peek is always crisp, and every arrival fades in gently instead of popping into place.

title: Critters hold their spots, plus new tricks
intent: On pages that finish loading in stages - like a video you're watching - critters used to jump to completely new hiding spots when the page settled. Now each critter stays with the exact button or card it chose and simply rides along if that spot moves. And tapping a critter has more surprises: alongside the wiggle, shiver, and hop, they can now twirl right around, duck down shyly, or do a squishy little bounce.

title: Shaved to the corner
intent: In the modern look, buttons and artwork have rounded corners - but a critter hiding behind them was cut along a square edge, so little squared-off shoulders could poke past the curve. Now the hidden part of a critter follows the exact rounded shape of whatever it's hiding behind, so every edge is clean and true to the button.

title: No more second positions
intent: The last flash is gone. When a page finished loading, it would quietly rebuild its buttons and cards behind the scenes - and critters treated the rebuilt copy as brand-new furniture, vanishing and reappearing somewhere else. Now a critter recognizes the rebuilt version of its hiding spot and stays exactly where it was, so what you see on first glance is what stays.

title: Every critter finds its voice
intent: Sound files no longer need matching names. A critter with its own matching sound still uses it, but any critter without one now borrows a voice from the sounds in your folder - and each keeps the same borrowed voice everywhere, so it feels like theirs. The plain beep only remains if the folder has no sounds at all.

title: Voice check
intent: A small diagnostic button in the Critters settings for when tap sounds aren't playing: it tests your sound files right on your device and says exactly what went wrong - for example when a sound file turns out to be in a format your phone can't play - instead of quietly falling back to the beep.

title: True colors, whole critters
intent: Uploaded critters now show their true colors: a leftover effect meant for the built-in figurines was quietly shifting the hues of your own images, so a beige rabbit could come out looking green - your art now renders exactly as the file is. And no critter ever gets cut off at the left or right edge of the screen anymore, on any page, no matter how the layout behaves.

title: A tidier Settings
intent: Settings gets a spring cleaning: two new pages at the bottom of the list gather what used to be scattered. Troubleshooting holds the diagnostic tools - the player's debug log and the critter sound check - and Experimental holds the adventurous switches like background audio, the lock-screen keep-alive, and custom player controls, each with its trade-offs spelled out. Everything works the same; it's just finally where you'd look for it.

title: Critters land in place
intent: The critters no longer flash in at odd spots and then jump behind things while a page loads. They now wait for the page to finish settling and appear once, already tucked into their final hiding spots - so they're in the right place from the moment you see them, on both desktop and phone.

title: Poke a critter, not the page
intent: On a computer, clicking a critter quickly no longer accidentally highlights the text next to it. You can poke and re-poke them as fast as you like and the page stays put - and a critter sitting over a link still lets your click through to open it.

title: Critters with more to say
intent: Critters that don't have their own assigned sound now take turns playing through all of your critter sound files, so tapping them gives a bit of variety instead of the same little beep every time. Critters you've paired with a specific sound still play that sound, and if you have no sound files at all you'll still get the friendly default beep.

title: Random critter sounds, your call
intent: There's a new switch in Settings under Critters: "Random sound each tap." Turn it on and any critter that doesn't have its own matching sound file will play a random one from your collection every time you poke it, for real variety. Leave it off (the default) and each of those critters keeps one consistent sound, exactly as before. Either way, a critter paired with its own sound always plays that. (This is the switch that actually makes the previous version's idea work - nothing to re-upload.)

title: A cleaner player, and Ambient mode
intent: The watch page gets tidier and more immersive. The redundant Previous/Next buttons under the video are gone - the player's own controls already do that. A Theatre button now sits as a small icon next to the gear, and Autoplay and Loop moved into that gear menu to declutter. And new: Ambient mode (in the gear menu, dark themes only) casts a soft, gently shifting glow behind the player in the colors of whatever's on screen - video or album art - for a more cinematic feel, just like YouTube. It's off by default; flip it on and enjoy. It's careful with battery, pausing itself whenever the video is paused or the tab is in the background.

title: Watch-page fixes
intent: Quick fixes to yesterday's watch-page update. Rotating your phone to landscape fills the screen properly again - the menu no longer sits on top of the video. Turning Theatre mode on now tucks the little critters into their new spots instead of leaving them stranded. And on the watch page the critters settle into place once the page has loaded, rather than popping in and then jumping around.

title: Critters sneak in, ambient dials down
intent: Four bits of polish. The critters now sneak in - a slow, soft fade with a gentle drift into place instead of popping onto the page. There's a new Size setting for them too: tiny, normal, large or extra large (note that the bigger ones need more room, so you'll see somewhat fewer of them, and they'll peek out further from behind small buttons). Ambient mode gets an amount picker in the player's gear menu - subtle, normal, intense or extreme - and it now defaults to a gentler level; pick Intense for exactly what you had before. And the ambient glow finally fades out softly at its edges like real light, instead of stopping on a hard line.

title: Ambient mode actually shows up
intent: Fixes yesterday's Ambient mode: the glow was there but mathematically hidden behind the video, so nothing rendered no matter which amount you picked. It now spreads properly around the player at every level, still fading out softly at its edges. Note that Intense matches the old spread but is gentler at the edge - that softness is the whole point of the fix - so if you want the strongest look, try Extreme.

title: Ambient mode stops interrupting playback
intent: On phones, turning Ambient mode on could make playback pause itself a few seconds in and drop the artwork from the lock screen and Dynamic Island. The glow was simply too expensive to draw - a big blurred layer being repainted far more often than it needed to be - so it has been made dramatically cheaper. Two honest notes: the glow is now a somewhat tighter halo around the player than yesterday's version (that softness was where the cost was), and while turning Ambient off definitely stopped the pausing, the exact reason your phone reacted that way is not yet confirmed - so please tell us if it still happens.

title: Popcorn theatre button, pill-shaped library buttons, and friendlier critters
intent: A handful of polish touches. The theatre-mode button on the watch page is now a little popcorn bucket, so it's clearer what it does. The buttons across the top of your library - Sort, Shuffle, Rescan and the All/Videos/Audio filters - now use the same rounded pill shape as the home feed's filter chips. Tapping one of the little critters always makes its sound now and never accidentally taps the thing behind it, and the critters no longer look upside-down when you've made them extra large and their whole body is showing. In dark mode, the Ambient glow now spills softly across the left menu bar instead of stopping in a hard line against it. And when a subscription checks a channel but nothing new comes down, the logs now spell out exactly why each video was skipped - so if a video you expected didn't download, there's finally a trail to follow (if that's happening to you, send us the log line and the video link).

title: The rounded pill buttons now cover the rest of your pages
intent: Following on from yesterday's library pills: the toolbars on your Books, Music, Podcasts and History pages now use the same rounded pill buttons, so the whole app feels consistent. Buttons that start something new - like Add or Subscribe - keep their bold accent colour so they still stand out; everything just gets the softer rounded shape. All of it follows your chosen theme's colours automatically, in light and dark.

title: Tapping inside an open menu no longer sets off a critter
intent: A small fix for the little critters. If one was peeking out from behind something and you opened a menu or dropdown on top of it, clicking inside that menu could set off the critter's sound - and sometimes even swallow your click so the menu didn't respond. Now a critter only reacts when you actually tap it out in the open, never when something else is drawn on top of it.

title: Theatre mode fits the screen, and the toolbar buttons match everywhere
intent: Two fixes. In theatre mode on a computer, if you also collapsed the left menu the video used to grow so tall it ran off the bottom of the screen; now it sizes to fit the window and centres, just like YouTube. And the rounded pill buttons across the app now match the weight of the ones on the home feed, so they look consistent whether you're on the home page, Downloads, Books, Music, Podcasts or History.

title: Friendlier critters and a clearer popcorn button
intent: A fun little batch for the critters. Tapping a critter now has a great variety of reactions - eighteen of them, from a nod or a wobble to a backflip or a tada - picked at random each time. When a critter is peeking out from behind a button, tapping the button now works as you'd expect instead of setting off the critter. Collapsing the left menu re-tucks the critters against the new layout so they don't hang in mid-air. And the theatre-mode button is now a clearer, taller popcorn bucket that matches the size of the settings gear next to it.

title: Critters: no more overlapping, fully solid, and no sideways scroll
intent: Three fixes for the critters. They no longer pile up on top of each other - when several would land in the same spot they now keep clear of one another instead of stacking. They also render fully solid again; some had looked faintly see-through, which wasn't intended. And your phone no longer scrolls a little sideways - a critter peeking near the edge of the screen had been nudging the page just past the edge.

title: Optionally let critters overlap a little
intent: A new experimental option under Settings, Critters. Since critters stopped overlapping entirely you may see fewer of them in tight spots, especially at the busiest density on a phone. Turn on "Let critters overlap a little" and they'll be allowed to lightly graze each other again, so you get more of them - but they still won't pile into a heavy stack. It's off by default; flip it on if you want a fuller crowd.

title: Two mobile fixes: critters stay put when you rotate, and a text-size glitch
intent: Two small fixes for your phone. When critters are on a page and you turn your phone and turn it back, they now stay right where they were instead of scattering to new spots. And the little "Playing on" card no longer shows oversized text after you come out of a full-screen video - its text stays the normal size.

title: Fix critters looking broken when you rotate your phone
intent: A quick follow-up. In the last update, turning your phone sideways could leave the little critters bunched up and looking broken down one edge of the screen. This undoes the change that caused it, so the critters behave normally again when you rotate - they simply settle into fresh spots, as they did before. The "Playing on" text-size fix from the last update stays.

title: Music now goes full screen when you turn your phone sideways
intent: On a video page, turning your phone to landscape while playing a song now expands the artwork to fill the screen, just like a video already did. Before, the music player tried to expand but stayed hidden behind the menus and header. This had been the case for a while; it's fixed now on that page.

title: No more accidental sideways scrolling while watching on your phone
intent: While watching something on your phone, the page could sometimes be dragged sideways a little when the glowing background effect was on. The page now stays put horizontally. The glow above and below the player is unchanged.

title: TV Shows are now a first-class library
intent: You can now add a TV Shows folder, right alongside your Videos, Music, Books and Podcasts. Point FileTube at a folder of shows laid out the usual way - a folder per show, a folder per season, episode files named like "House MD S02E22 - Forever" - and it builds a wall of show posters for you. Tap a show to see its seasons and episodes, then tap an episode to play it right there. A picture placed in a show's folder becomes its poster; if there isn't one, FileTube makes a poster and per-episode thumbnails from the video itself. Episodes in a format your browser can't play - including ones that just use a codec it doesn't understand - are converted on the fly, exactly like the rest of your videos. The Shows tab only appears once you've added a Shows folder. Remembering where you left off in an episode and a "Continue watching" row are coming in a follow-up update.

title: Find Shows in Playlists on your phone, and pick its icon
intent: A quick follow-up to the new TV Shows library. On your phone, Shows now shows up in the Playlists list alongside Music, Books and Podcasts - before, it was hard to reach there. And you can now choose the icon for Shows from Settings, just like you can for your other libraries.

title: TV episodes now play in the full player, and remember where you left off
intent: A big upgrade for TV Shows. Tapping an episode now opens it in the same full player your videos use - so you get the mini-player, the episode title, and Previous/Next buttons that move through the whole show in order, plus autoplay and loop. It also remembers where you left off in each episode and picks up right there next time, and a new "Continue watching" row on the Shows home puts your half-finished episodes one tap away. Admins can now set a show's poster right from the app - open a show and tap "Change poster" to upload your own image. One thing to know: keeping an episode's audio playing with the screen off isn't available yet (video already had this), though the lock-screen play/pause/skip controls do work.

title: TV episodes now use your themed player on the phone
intent: A quick follow-up. On your phone, TV episodes were showing the plain built-in player controls instead of the themed player your videos use. Now episodes use the same themed player as everything else. If you don't see the themed controls, check Settings and turn on "custom player on mobile" - that's the switch for both videos and episodes.

title: TV episodes get the full treatment: show info, background audio, ambient, and fixes
intent: Four finishing touches for TV Shows. An episode's page now shows its details like a video does - the file name, when it was added, its size and type - and the show itself sits where the channel would be, with its poster as the little round icon; tap it to jump back to that show. Episode audio can now keep playing when you lock your phone, just like videos (it uses the same "Background audio for video" setting - flip it on in Settings if you haven't). Ambient mode - and the autoplay, loop, and theatre controls in the player's gear menu - now work on episodes too; they'd been missing there. And tapping the mini-player to get back to an episode no longer flashes a "Failed to Load Media" error.

title: Ambient mode now really works on TV episodes
intent: A quick follow-up to yesterday's TV update. Ambient mode on an episode looked like it turned on but never actually glowed - a behind-the-scenes error stopped it right as it started. That's fixed: turn on Ambient in the player's gear menu while watching an episode in a dark theme and the soft glow now appears around the player, just like it does for videos.

title: TV episode pages, tidied up
intent: A round of polish for episode pages. The Subscribe button no longer appears next to a show's name (shows aren't channels), and the "File Path" line - which used to sit there loading forever - now shows the episode's file name. Episodes also get the same nostalgic fake comments as everything else, and you can add your own. And the "Change poster" button is gone: to set a show's poster, just drop an image named poster.jpg (or folder/cover/show .jpg/.png/.webp) into the show's folder - FileTube picks it up automatically.

title: Episode pages now show what's up next
intent: The sidebar on an episode page now lists the rest of the show, in order - the episodes that come after the one you're watching, and once those run out it wraps back around to episode 1, so there's always something to tap next. Each card shows the episode's thumbnail, its number and title, and its length. The episode you're currently watching isn't listed.

title: Choose whether the Shows page shows Continue watching
intent: A small option that was missing: Settings now has a checkbox called Show Continue watching on the Shows page, right next to the one for the home page. Untick it and the Shows page goes straight to your poster wall with no Continue row. The two checkboxes are independent, so you can keep the row on one page and not the other. Like the other row toggles, this is a per-browser preference.

title: Your TV shows are on the Roku now
intent: The Roku channel's Libraries picker (press Left on the grid) has a new Shows entry: a poster wall of your shows. Pick a show, then a season - a show with only one season jumps straight to its episodes - then an episode, and it plays like any video, with Next, Previous, autoplay, and loop moving through the season in order. Resume stays in sync across your screens: stop an episode on the TV and your phone or browser offers to pick up where you left off, and finishing one on the TV marks it watched everywhere. To get it, redeploy the channel to your Roku from this version.

title: The Roku Shows wall looks right now
intent: The first screen of Shows on the Roku - the wall of posters - got a cleanup. The posters are bigger, so they actually look like posters from across the room. A long show name now wraps onto a second line instead of getting cut off or running over the text beneath it. And the season and episode counts sit on their own separate lines instead of crowding together. Redeploy the channel to your Roku from this version to get it.

title: Roku Shows wall: text no longer overlaps
intent: A follow-up to the last Roku change: the show name and the season/episode counts were still overlapping each other on the poster wall. Now each show's name sits on its own line and the two count lines sit cleanly below it, the same tidy way the video grid already looks. A really long show name is trimmed with an ellipsis at the edge of its poster instead of running over the text beneath it. Redeploy the channel to your Roku from this version to get it.

title: Transcript: read, copy or share a video's captions as text
intent: Any video that has captions now has a Transcript button next to Share. On a computer it opens the full transcript in a text box - the video's title, the date it was published and the channel at the top, then everything that was said, one line at a time - with a Copy button and an optional toggle to show a time next to each line. On a phone the same button opens the share sheet so you can send the transcript straight to Notes, Messages or an AI app, or copy it to the clipboard. YouTube's auto-generated captions repeat every line two or three times as they scroll; the transcript shows each line once. Videos without captions do not get the button, and TV episodes are not covered yet.

title: Share a transcript with your AI app, plus a tidier transcript and action bar
intent: The Transcript button gains a Share with AI option. Under Settings, Transcript sharing, you write one or more prompts (a summary request, an analysis request, whatever you usually ask) and give each a name; when you share a transcript with AI, your prompt is placed in front of the transcript in the share sheet, so you can pick Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT or any other app and it gets your request and the text together. If you have several prompts you choose one by name; with none set up the option simply does not appear. On a computer without a share sheet the button copies the prompt and transcript for pasting. Also: with timestamps off the transcript now reads as flowing paragraphs instead of one line per caption, and on a desktop the row of buttons under a video stays on one line (showing icons only when the column is narrow) instead of spilling onto a second row outside theatre mode.

title: A tidier row of buttons under every video, draggable AI prompts, and channel attribution as an opt-in
intent: The buttons under a video are now two tiers: Like, Share, Transcript and Queue stay in the row, and a More button opens the rest (Play next, Download, Delete, Move, Mark watched and any others) in the same pick-one style the app already uses. On a phone that is five icons on one line instead of ten; on a wide screen every button still shows with its name. In Settings, your Share with AI prompts can now be dragged into whatever order you like (grab the handle; arrow keys work too). And the Attribute button, which helps re-file older downloads that were saved under the wrong channel, is now off by default - turn it on under Settings, Experimental if your library needs it; it also has a proper icon at last.

title: Button names on your phone, and Transcript on the cards
intent: The row of buttons under a video on your phone now shows the words - Queue, Like, Share, Transcript - with a small ... button for the rest, all on one line. And Transcript can now sit on the video cards themselves: under Settings, Card corners, pick Transcript for any corner and every video that has captions gets the button right on its card, opening the same transcript view - read it, copy it, share it, or send it to your AI app with your prompt - without opening the video first.

title: A fourth spot for controls on your video cards
intent: The little controls in the corners of your video tiles can now use the bottom-right corner too. Under Settings, Card corners, you'll find a fourth picker - Bottom right - next to the other three; put Like, Share, Transcript or any control there, or leave it empty. The running time still lives in that corner, and when you place a control beside it the time simply slides over to make room. It's off by default, so nothing on your cards changes until you choose to use it.

title: One search box for everything
intent: The search box at the top now looks across your whole library at once - not just videos, but music, podcasts (both shows and individual episodes), your TV shows and episodes, and books - all in one list of results, each with a little label telling you what kind of thing it is. A row of filters (All, Videos, Audio, Music, Podcasts, Shows, Books) lets you narrow to one kind with a tap. The best matches come first: an exact title beats a partial one, whatever kind it is. Type a name and everything you have that matches shows up together.

title: The video length matches its buttons - and stays put
intent: A small polish on the video tiles: the little running-time label (like 11:10) is now the same size as the buttons in the corners, instead of looking a bit smaller, so the row lines up evenly. And when a tile plays its short hover preview, the running time no longer disappears behind it - you can still see how long something is while the preview plays.

title: A softer, tidier running-time label
intent: Following up on the last tweak: the running-time label on a video tile is no longer bold, so it sits more quietly, and its little background is now the exact same shade as the buttons in the corners - so the whole row of pills looks like one matching set.

title: Quieter behind-the-scenes upkeep
intent: Housekeeping you won't see: small, low-risk updates to the pieces the app is built from now apply themselves automatically once everything still passes, so the app stays current and secure with less manual fuss. Bigger or riskier updates still wait for a human to look them over. Nothing changes in how the app looks or works.

title: Play a song, see its album
intent: When you play a song - from search, a card, or the song list - the music view now opens that song's album, so the rest of the album is right there to keep listening (and next/previous walk the album). Even better, it sticks: pop out to the mini-player and tap back into the song, and you land on the album again instead of the default view. Songs with no album just play as before.

title: See how long it is, right in notifications
intent: The little thumbnail on each notification now shows the length in its corner - the same small time tag you see on the video tiles. So when a channel posts something new, you can tell at a glance whether it's a quick one-minute clip or a full-length video (or podcast episode) before you even open it - handy for deciding what to keep and what to clear.

title: Tap away to close search
intent: A little less fuss: if you open the search bar and then change your mind, just tap anywhere outside it (like the home button) and it closes on its own - no need to press the search button again. If you've already typed something, it stays put so you don't lose your search.

title: Your downloaded music, in the Music library
intent: If you download MP3s from music channels - game-music remixes, album mixes, that kind of thing - you can now have them show up in the Music library too, grouped by channel and played through the music player, without duplicating anything or taking them out of your feed. It's off by default: turn it on in Settings, and channels whose uploads are tagged as music appear on their own. For the ones YouTube files under something else (a game-music channel it labels 'Gaming', say), just tap the little music note on that channel's page to include it. Great for a nostalgia library of full albums you've downloaded.

title: Pick your music channels in one place
intent: A cleaner take on downloaded music in your library. A channel is now either fully in your Music library or not - no more a single stray song showing up while the rest of the channel stays hidden. Channels that are mostly music switch on by themselves; for everything else there's a new 'Channels in Music' list in Settings where you flip a channel on and get all of its songs, future downloads included. One obvious place to manage it, instead of hunting for a control on each channel's page.

title: A fresh look for Music: artist circles + Jump back in
intent: The Music library gets the first piece of a bigger redesign. Your artists now show as round picture tiles using each channel's own avatar, so you can spot who you're after at a glance (ripped albums with no channel keep their cover art). And a new 'Jump back in' row sits across the top with whatever you were last playing, so you're one tap from picking up where you left off. More of the redesign - a proper album page and a nicer now-playing screen - is on the way.

title: A redesigned Music page: a home of shelves, every artist a circle
intent: Music gets a real redesign. It now opens on a Home of scrollable shelves - your artists and your recently-added albums, each with a 'See all' to open the full list - instead of a flat grid. And every artist is now a round tile: channels use their picture, and your own ripped albums use their cover art, so the whole artist wall is circular and consistent. Albums, Artists, and Songs are still there as full lists. Same colours as the rest of the app - just a cleaner, more browsable layout.

title: Less friction in Music: a list view, sortable songs, recent artists
intent: Making Music quicker to get around. The artist tiles are smaller now, and there's a new button to flip the Artists view between round pictures and a compact list - so you can scan down and tap the artist you want instead of swiping past big circles. When you open an artist, their songs can now be sorted, and default to release date for anything you downloaded from YouTube (instead of a random order). And a 'Recently played' row up top on Home puts whoever you've been listening to one tap away.

title: Music fixes: your downloads now show in Recently played
intent: Three fixes for Music. Artists you downloaded from YouTube now show up in the 'Recently played' and 'Jump back in' rows after you listen to them - before, only your ripped albums did, and your downloads were quietly left out. A little critter that was sitting on top of the Shuffle button and getting in the way is gone - the critters now stay off the toolbar controls. And a stray view-switch button that showed up on an album's song list (where it did nothing) no longer appears there.

title: Critters stay off the now-playing screen
intent: A quick fix following the last one: a critter could sit over the title and the Up-next list on the expanded now-playing screen in Music. Now the whole now-playing panel is off-limits to the critters, so nothing drapes over your song title or the queue. (Same fix covers the Podcasts now-playing screen.) The critters still pop up from your artwork and cards as before - just never on top of the controls.

title: Back button keeps you inside Music
intent: Opening an album or artist in Music, or tapping a song to play it, used to be a one-way trip: pressing Back (or swiping back from the edge on your phone) jumped you all the way out of Music. Now Back steps you back where you'd expect - out of the album to your list, and back through an artist to where you started - and only leaves Music once you're at the top. Your music keeps playing the whole time. (Podcasts, Shows and Books will get the same treatment in upcoming updates.)

title: The same smart Back arrives in Podcasts and Shows
intent: Following last update's Music change: Podcasts and Shows now do the same thing. Open a podcast or a show and press Back (or swipe back from the edge) and you step back to your list instead of jumping out of the section - and it only leaves once you're back at the grid. Books already worked this way. So Back now behaves consistently wherever you are in your library.

title: The little critters stay put on scrolling rows
intent: A small visual fix: if you have the critters turned on, one sitting on a scrolling row (like Music's 'Recently played') used to stay stuck in place while the row slid underneath it, which looked off. Now it rides along with the card it's perched on, so it stays where it belongs as you scroll.

title: Critters stay off the sliding rows entirely
intent: A follow-up to last update: making the critters ride the scrolling rows still looked a bit off, so now they simply don't appear on those horizontal sliding rows at all (like Music's 'Recently played' or the books shelf). They still pop up everywhere else - on your cards, tiles and artwork - just not on the rows that slide.

title: Downloaded mixes and full-album files become albums in Music
intent: If you download a long audio file that has chapters - a DJ mix, a full album, a live set - Music now treats it as an album: each chapter shows up as its own track you can tap, and you can search for a chapter by name and jump straight to it. Tapping a chapter starts playing right at that spot in the file. This only applies to downloaded audio you've chosen to include in Music. One thing to know for now: once a chapter starts it keeps playing into the next one rather than stopping at the chapter's end, and it always starts a chapter from the beginning.

title: Polish for the new Music albums: artwork, album in search, and picking up where you left off
intent: A round of polish for the chaptered-album feature. Those albums now show the real artwork from the file instead of a grey square. Music search now shows the album name next to each song, not just the artist. When you play one of these albums it shows up in 'Recently played' and picks up where you left off, so the artists you listen to are one tap away on the Music home. And on a desktop screen there's a new theatre button that puts the album's track list beside the player, filling the empty space to the right.

title: New downloads show up in Recently added, and Next Up keeps the whole list
intent: Two Music tweaks. New albums you download now show up at the top of 'Recently added' where you'd expect them, instead of getting buried - so freshly grabbed mixes and albums are easy to find and play. And the 'Next Up' list no longer shrinks as a song plays: it now shows the whole queue, with the tracks you've already played dimmed but still tappable, so you can jump back to one anytime.

title: Music now-playing polish: jump to the song you picked, tidier Up next, and the Music toggle on channels
intent: A few small Music fixes. When you pick a song, the Up next list now scrolls straight to it so you can see what's playing without hunting. The Up next list is now a neat scrollable panel that always shows full rows instead of getting cut off at the bottom. And the little music-note button that adds a channel to your Music library now appears when you open a channel from the home, not only from the Downloads folder view.

title: Up next settles on the playing song, and the Music toggle works on pinned channels
intent: Two follow-up fixes. When you pick a song, the Up next list now stays put on the playing track instead of scrolling to it and then jumping away as the rest of the list fills in. And the little music-note button that adds a channel to your Music library now shows up when you click one of your pinned channels in the sidebar, not just when you reach a channel from the home.

title: No more layout jump in the wide Music player when you come back to a song
intent: A polish fix for the wide (theatre) Music player on desktop. When you tapped the mini-player to come back to what's playing, the page looked right for a moment and then the 'Jump back in' row jumped downward as the track list filled in. Now the track list scrolls inside its own panel instead of pushing the rest of the page around, so everything stays where it lands - no jump.

title: Pick how the Music player looks on your phone: Apple Music, Spotify, or iPod
intent: The full-screen Music player on your phone now comes in three looks you can switch between right from the now-playing screen: an Apple-Music-style big-art view, a Spotify-style dark view, and a warm retro iPod view. Pick whichever feels right - it's remembered on your device. It's phone-only; the desktop player is unchanged. Under the hood it's the same player as before, so background play and your lock-screen controls keep working exactly as they did. This is a first cut of the look, so expect some polishing to come.

title: The three phone Music skins now really look different from each other
intent: The first cut of the phone Music skins felt like the same player in three colours. Now each one has its own layout: Apple is all about the cover art, with a big blurred backdrop and one large play button; Spotify is a bold dark screen with a green play button and your up-next queue right there with little cover thumbnails; and iPod is a proper throwback, with a brushed-metal top bar, a framed cover, a chunky metal button cluster, and a classic blue track list. Also fixed a small annoyance: the page no longer scrolls behind the full-screen player. It's still phone-only and still the same player underneath, so background play and lock-screen controls are unchanged.

title: Switch your phone Music skin from the account menu
intent: Changing your phone Music skin is now done from the account menu (the avatar menu at the top): there's a 'Music skin' row with Apple, Spotify, and iPod to pick from, and the player updates right away. The little skin buttons that used to sit inside the player have been removed - they were hard to see against some of the skins, so switching now has one clear home. It's a per-device choice on your phone, and it only appears in the menu on the Music page and the home screen (where the skins live). Nothing else about playback changes.

title: The Music-skin picker is now on the Settings page
intent: Picking your phone Music skin now lives on the Settings page, under Appearance, right next to the Theme and Icons options - Apple Music, Spotify, or iPod, with the current one highlighted. This replaces the version that briefly lived in the account menu, which often didn't show up depending on which page you'd opened first. It's a per-device choice and it applies to the Music player on your phone; you can set it from your computer or your phone. Nothing else about playback changes.

title: The iPod skin is now a real iPod - with a working click wheel
intent: The iPod Music skin got a big glow-up to look and feel like a real iPod Classic: a glossy white body, the classic Now Playing screen with your cover art, song details and star rating, the shiny blue progress bar, and a gray click wheel underneath. The wheel's buttons actually work - the center is play/pause, the sides skip tracks, and MENU steps back (and backs you all the way out of the player). Tap MENU or the center to bring up your song list and tap any song to play it. Across all three skins, the buttons that didn't do anything are gone, Shuffle now really shuffles, and the player fills the whole screen instead of leaving the app's top bar showing. It's still phone-only and the same player underneath, so background play and lock-screen controls are unchanged.

title: iPod skin polish: right-sized screen, crisp buttons, glossy finish
intent: A few finishing touches on the iPod Music skin. The screen is now the right, compact size instead of stretching down the page, so the proportions match a real iPod. The rewind, forward and play icons on the click wheel are now crisp gray icons instead of the blue emoji they were showing as. And the body and wheel got the classic glossy iPod sheen. Just polish - it works the same as before.

title: A black iPod skin, scrolling song titles, and a smoother wheel
intent: Three additions to the phone Music player. There's now a black iPod to choose in Settings alongside the silver one - same classic look, space-black body and wheel. Long song, artist and album names on the iPod now gently scroll so you can read the whole thing, just like a real iPod (and they hold still if you've turned on Reduce Motion). And the little grey flash that showed when you tapped the click wheel is gone, so the wheel feels smooth. Phone-only, same player underneath - background play and lock-screen controls are unchanged.

title: Music-skin polish and playful new names
intent: A round of polish for the phone Music skins. The iPod screen now stays a fixed size no matter how long your song list is (it used to stretch when you opened the list). The scrolling song titles now work on the Apple- and Spotify-style skins too, not just the iPod. The Apple skin's little bar for closing the player is easier to tap, and the Spotify skin's play button is now properly centered. And the four skins got fun names instead of the brand names: Cider, Nordic, Pocket Classic, and Pocket Classic (Black). Nothing about playback changes.

title: The silver iPod skin gets its glossy shine
intent: The silver Pocket Classic Music skin now has the glossy iPod shine the black one already had - a bright highlight across the top and a soft shadow along the bottom edge give it that classic reflective, polished look. Just a visual touch-up on that one skin.

title: The page stays put behind the full-screen Music player
intent: Fixed an annoyance in the full-screen phone Music player: dragging on the body of the player (anywhere that isn't the screen or the wheel) used to make the page behind it scroll. Now the player holds the page still, while the song list and the Spotify-style queue still scroll normally. Also toned down the shine on the black iPod skin so it's a little more subtle. Just polish - nothing about playback changes.

title: Smoother seek bar when you skip tracks
intent: When you skipped to the previous or next track on a phone Music skin, the progress bar would briefly show the old track's position and then jump - a little jarring. Now it resets cleanly to the start the moment you skip and fills up as the new track plays, the way you'd expect.

title: The iPod song list shows the whole album and jumps to your current song
intent: On the iPod Music skin, opening the song list (the center button) now shows the whole album and lands on the song you're playing, so you can scroll up to earlier tracks and down to later ones. Before, the list started near your current song, so you could only browse earlier tracks if you were on the very first one. Tap any song to play it, same as before.

title: The iPod click wheel really spins
intent: The iPod Music skin's click wheel now works like the real thing. Open the song list and spin your thumb around the wheel to scroll through your songs - a highlight moves song to song, and a quick flick jumps further. Press the center button to play the highlighted song. It's a much more fun, hands-on way to pick a track on your phone.

title: Pop the music player out into a floating window
intent: On a computer, you can now pop the music player out into its own little window - your chosen skin, like the iPod, floating on its own. In Chrome and Edge it stays on top of everything so you can keep it in the corner while you work in other windows; in other browsers it opens as a normal movable window you can park anywhere. Look for the new 'Pop out' button while music is playing. (On phones, tapping a track already gives you the full-screen skin, so the button is desktop-only.)

title: Spin the pop-out iPod wheel to change the volume
intent: In the floating iPod player on your computer, you can now spin the click wheel to change the volume - clockwise for louder - with a volume bar that pops up just like the real thing. Also fixed: the time in the floating window used to freeze; now it keeps ticking smoothly while a song plays.

title: Downloaded music opens in the music player
intent: Tap a downloaded song or album anywhere - your home feed, search, a channel, or continue-watching - and it now opens in the music player instead of the video page. Albums with chapters open as an album, so you can browse the tracks. There's a new setting, 'Open downloaded music in the music player' (on by default), if you ever want to turn it off. Regular videos are unaffected.

title: The song title keeps up as an album plays
intent: When an album plays straight through from one chapter to the next on its own, the now-playing title, the artwork, and the highlighted track in the list now update to the song that's actually playing - before, they'd stay stuck on the previous track unless you tapped ahead by hand. It works the same in the music view and the pop-out player. The iPod's click wheel is also a bit bigger now.

title: A sticker on the player for speed, loop, and skin
intent: There's a new little sticker in the corner of the music player (and the pop-out window). Tap it and you get quick controls for playback speed, loop, and switching between the Apple, Spotify, and iPod skins - all in one place, without leaving the player. You can also change the sticker itself in Settings > Appearance: keep the FileTube logo, pick an emoji, or upload your own small image.

title: A bigger iPod wheel you can spin to scrub
intent: The iPod skin's click wheel is now bigger, sized like a real iPod Classic's. And on your phone, you can spin the wheel while a song is playing to scrub through it - turn clockwise to jump forward, counter-clockwise to go back, and let go to land there. (On a computer the pop-out wheel still controls volume, which phones can't do.)

title: Loop a single track in an album, and a stick-on sticker
intent: Turning on Loop for one song inside a downloaded album now repeats just that song, instead of playing on through the rest of the album. And the player sticker got two touches: if you use your own image (or the logo) it's no longer squeezed into a circle - it shows as-is - and it sits at a slight, playful tilt like a real peel-and-stick sticker. Emoji stickers keep their round badge.

title: Resize and angle your player sticker
intent: The player sticker is a bit bigger now, and you can make it your own: in Settings > Appearance > Player sticker, pick a size (default, 2x, 3x, or a big 5x) and a tilt (straight, or leaning left or right). Changing the size keeps your chosen image or emoji, and vice versa.

title: All your audio, right in the music player
intent: Anything you've downloaded that's audio-only now shows up in the music player automatically - no setting to flip, it's just there. Tap a song anywhere and it opens in the player, no detour through the video page. If you'd rather keep a particular channel out of Music, you can switch it off in Settings. Also new: on the iPod skin, press and hold the rewind or fast-forward button to scan through a track - hold to sweep, let go to land where you want.

title: Music player polish
intent: A few nice touches to the phone music player: holding the wheel no longer accidentally highlights text like it's a web page, and spinning to scrub is now much finer and smoother so you can land exactly where you want. Tapping a song from the home feed now drops you straight into the player instead of flashing the music list on the way. The extra-large (5x) sticker size is gone since it covered the wheel - the other sizes and tilts stay.

title: Album art that fits, and a smoother open
intent: Album covers that aren't square (a lot of YouTube ones) now show in full in the music skins, with a soft blurred version of the same art filling the space around them instead of being cropped - it looks a lot more polished. And tapping a song from the home feed now really does open straight into the player, with no flash of the music list on the way in.

title: Search with the keyboard's Return key
intent: On an iPhone you can now just press Return on the keyboard to run a search - no more reaching over to tap the Search button. The keyboard's return key even says "Search" now.

title: Podcasts get the iPod player, and audio opens there from everywhere
intent: Podcasts now play in the same slick mobile player that music uses - the click-wheel scrolls the episode list and scrubs the timeline, with the show's art full-screen. And any audio, whether you tap it in search or from a notification, now opens straight in that player instead of the plain video page.

title: The player's back button returns you where you started
intent: Open the mobile player from Home, a search, or a tab, then press back - it now tucks the player into the corner and takes you right back to where you launched it from, instead of leaving you on some other page. Skipping tracks doesn't change where back takes you.

title: Critters stop misbehaving on the music page
intent: The little decorative critters no longer show up in odd spots, pile on top of each other, or disappear on the music page. They now stay out of the way while the full-screen player is open and settle back into place properly as you move around the music page.

title: Every video action, right on the music player
intent: The full-screen music player's sticker menu now has an Extras page with everything the video watch page offers: share the original YouTube link (including at the current moment), download the file, like it, mark it watched, add it to the queue or play it next, read the transcript, refresh its details from YouTube, move it to another folder, or delete it - all without leaving the player. It appears for music that came from YouTube, and each option only shows when it actually applies to the playing track.

title: One player engine everywhere, and the classic wheel now scrubs on desktop
intent: Under the hood, the music player and the podcast player now share one engine, so they look and behave the same and future player features arrive in both at once. Two things you can feel right away: spinning the classic wheel in the desktop pop-out now scrubs through the song exactly like it does on your phone (instead of changing the volume), and the podcast player picked up the quick menu (speed, loop, skin) plus hold-to-fast-forward/rewind on the wheel. This also fixes a case where opening Music from certain pages on a phone could show the plain player instead of your chosen skin.

title: Audio opens the right player from everywhere, and the desktop podcast player catches up
intent: Tapping anything that is purely audio - from a pinned channel, your history, the notification bell, the queue, or a watch page's related list - now opens the music player instead of sometimes landing in the video player. Older audio downloads that were misbehaving this way heal automatically after your next library scan, so give it one scan before judging. The desktop podcast player also caught up with the music player: the full up-next episode list with your place marked (and earlier episodes one tap away), the theatre layout beside the player, and the pop-out floating window.

title: Listen to any video like a song, and a menu built for thumbs
intent: Every video's watch page now has a Listen button: it plays the video as audio in the full music player - skins, wheel, the whole experience - perfect for talks and long videos you just want to hear. The menu's first page has a Watch button to jump back to the video exactly where you are; your place is shared both ways. One honest caveat: videos of ten minutes or less start from the beginning when you switch to Listen. Also, the music player's sticker menu got much bigger buttons - everything is now sized for a thumb, so picking speed, loop, a skin, or an Extra no longer takes surgical precision.

title: Listen mode gets its finishing touches
intent: Three quick fixes from the first day of Listen mode. The music player now shows the video's actual thumbnail as the cover art instead of a gray placeholder. The watch page's button row fits on one line again on phones - the Queue button moved into the More menu to make room for Listen. And the mini player now remembers which mode you're in: tap it after switching between Listen and Watch and it takes you back to the right one, not the one you left earlier. One known quirk remains: right after switching from Listen back to Watch, a finished video may jump to the next one even if autoplay is off, and rotating the phone can behave oddly - leaving and reopening the video clears it.

title: The music keeps playing
intent: Play one song and the player no longer just stops at the end. When your queue runs out - a single track, the last song of an album, the end of a shuffle - FileTube quietly lines up a few more: songs by the same artist first, then good neighbors from your library, skipping anything you've already heard this session. You can see exactly what's coming in the up-next list and skip anything you don't want. It's on by default for music; a new Autoplay switch in the player's sticker menu turns it off and remembers your choice. Podcasts and videos you're listening to are left alone - they still end where they end.

title: The sticker menu joins the family
intent: The music player's sticker menu now looks like it belongs: the same font as the rest of the app (it was quietly using the browser's default), proper weights, and little icons on each row that match the ones you know from the watch page - Watch, Loop, Autoplay, Extras, and all the Extras actions. Selected options glow the app's red instead of flipping to white. The Extras page is taller so its whole action list fits without scrolling. And on the Pocket Classic skin, the progress bar traded its flat blue for a glossy old-school macOS aqua glass, sitting in a properly shadowed groove.

title: The click wheel actually clicks
intent: Spin the Pocket Classic's wheel on your iPhone and you now feel it: a real physical tick under your thumb about every four and a half degrees, just like the old iPod's click wheel - denser and buzzier the faster you flick. It works while browsing songs and while scrubbing through a track. This was long thought impossible for a web app on modern iPhones; a deep dive into the browser's own machinery found the one path that still works, and it was confirmed on-device before being built in. Everything else about the wheel - the buttons, hold-to-fast-forward, taps - behaves exactly as before, and phones or computers without the capability are completely unaffected.

title: The wheel's buttons are back, and the ticks got hotter
intent: Two quick follow-ups from the first hands-on with the clicking wheel. The Menu, back, forward, and play buttons work again - a quirk in how iPhones report taps on the invisible tick-maker was sending every button press to the center Select, and taps are now tracked by where your finger actually landed. And the ticking itself is more aggressive: a third denser than before, past even the original iPod's click rate, so a fast flick really buzzes.

title: Click wheel, Classic calibration
intent: The wheel's ticking is dialed to match the original iPod Classic exactly: 96 clicks per full turn - between the first version's gentler feel and the last one's too-hot buzz. This is the real hardware's own number, so a spin should now feel like the genuine article.

title: The Tray Player
intent: A new optional desktop mode: pop the player out, open its sticker menu, and flip on Tray - the window becomes a little iPod-Nano-style now-playing screen, sized to park in the corner just above your taskbar. Album art, song and artist, the status bar with its battery, and the glossy progress bar, all in a glanceable strip that floats over your apps but never covers the taskbar or the clock. Drag it to your corner once and the browser remembers the spot; the player reopens in whichever mode you last used. Works in Chrome and Edge on Windows and macOS.

title: Tray Player, Nano edition
intent: The corner player now really looks like a little iPod Nano. Its screen sits inset in the player's aluminum body, the whole thing is rounded like the real shell, and it comes in two colorways - silver and black. Open the tray's sticker menu and a new Color section switches between them on the spot (your pick doubles as your player skin everywhere). It's also a touch smaller overall, per the first hands-on.

title: Tray touches
intent: Two touches from the first hands-on with the Nano tray. The progress bar now responds to a mouse click - click anywhere on it to jump there, in the tray and on the phone's Pocket Classic screen alike. And the tray's sticker menu, which was getting squeezed into an unusable sliver by the tiny window, now opens across the whole tray - with a new nicety everywhere: tapping any empty space in the menu closes it.
